# JSON and Data Formats

## Overview
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the language that automations use to move data around, so being fluent in it is essential. It is just text organized in a very predictable way. The two building blocks are objects, written with curly braces { } and made of key-value pairs like "name": "Alice", and arrays, written with square brackets [ ] and holding an ordered list of items. Values can be strings (text in quotes), numbers, booleans (true/false), null (empty), or another object or array nested inside - which is how JSON represents complex data like a customer with a list of orders, each order having its own items. When an API responds, it almost always sends JSON, and when you configure an automation step you are usually picking values out of that JSON (the customer's email is at data.customer.email) or building JSON to send. You will constantly navigate nested structures, so learning to read a path like results[0].address.city - meaning the city of the first result's address - becomes second nature. It helps to compare JSON with other formats: CSV is a flat spreadsheet-like format good for tabular data, and XML is an older tag-based format still used by some enterprise systems, but JSON's readability and simplicity made it the default for modern APIs and automation tools. Mastering JSON now means you will never be confused when a workflow shows you raw data.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: What JSON is and why it is everywhere; Objects, arrays, and key-value pairs; Data types: string, number, boolean, null; Nested and array data; JSON vs CSV vs XML. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Take a real API response (from Day 3) and by hand write out the path to three different values inside it, including at least one that is inside an array and one that is deeply nested.
Mini Project: Create a JSON document describing a small e-commerce order: a customer object, an array of products (each with name, price, quantity), and a nested shipping address, then validate it with an online JSON validator.
Assignment: Convert a small table of data into both JSON and CSV, then write a few sentences on when you would choose each format.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

- Read any research papers linked for deeper theory.
- Prepare questions for tomorrow's module.

- Check the GitHub repositories for working code examples.
